entries.title: Psalms 63:1
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Early - Heb. in the morning, Which implies the doing it with diligence and speed. Thirsteth - For the enjoyment of thee in thy house and ordinances. Flesh - The desire of my soul, is so vehement, that my very body feels the effects of it. No water - In a land where I want the refreshing waters of the sanctuary.

entries.title: Psalms 63:2
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: To see - To enjoy. Power - The powerful and glorious effects of thy gracious presence.

entries.title: Psalms 63:5
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Satisfied - When thou shalt fulfil my earnest desire of enjoying thee in the sanctuary.

entries.title: Psalms 63:10
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Foxes - Their carcases shall become a prey to wild and ravenous creatures.

entries.title: Psalms 63:11–64:5
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The king - I who am already anointed king. Every one - That sweareth by the name of God, in truth, and judgment, and righteousness. Every sincere servant and worshipper of God. Shall glory - Shall rejoice in my deliverance.
